blockers.quote: That's the scholarship letter. You made the cut. And a paper card just opened over a stranger, with a number she couldn't see.
blockers.why: Check #3 fails: the title question lands around 0:36, and the friend/stakes arrive after 0:30.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 36–38 with: “What if good news showed who wants you to fail? Your best friend hears everything first. He always has.” Reduce the day montage to one two-second insert so -84 lands before 0:30.

blockers.quote: Two years of trash talk, and you get minus six? So what does a real red take?
blockers.why: Check #17 fails: roughly 95 seconds pass without a stake jump while the script cycles through tests.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “Two years of trash talk: minus six. Your best friend: minus eighty-four. Whatever red means, the dangerous number is at the next desk.”

blockers.quote: A thousand strangers. A thousand zeros. A few teal. And three red. All by the snack shop. All from your class.
blockers.why: Check #11 fails: the narration inventories exactly what the shot already shows instead of turning its meaning.
blockers.fix: Replace with: “You asked a thousand strangers to prove your friend was the exception. Instead, every red points back to your class.”

suggestions.quote: We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below (c10).
suggestions.fix: Put the rival and best friend comparison from line 163 between this fact and c12, so each fact becomes ammunition for a separate story observation.

suggestions.quote: In studies of regret, the most common is education: about a third of all regrets (c11).
suggestions.fix: Add the causal bridge: “But the person who paid for your classroom is still waiting. Across eleven studies, education is the most common life regret—about a third of all regrets (c11).”

suggestions.quote: So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Tie the question to the final image and leave faster: “Would you look up? Tell us in the comments.” Let the visual end card carry like and subscribe.

keep.quote: The card gets two minutes. It doesn't get to choose what you do next.
She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
That half-second is the other life, going past.
